answer: Reputation glacier: each identity’s score decays slowly, like ice calving at a vertex where trust accumulates, so a fresh clone starts near zero and must wait out the melt. An operator who spawns many wallets sees every parallel identity climb the same slow curve, and any flagged cluster freezes the operator’s payout address across all copies at dawn of the next settlement. Before that freeze triggers, the attacker pays roughly one full identity’s compute and time cost per clone, with no shortcut through volume.
